cards.text: Jesus has just been baptized, and a voice from heaven said, “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.” (Luke 3:21-22) Now, full of the Holy Spirit, Jesus heads back from the Jordan. You'd expect a parade next, friend, but the Spirit leads Him somewhere else.

cards.question: Full of the Holy Spirit, Jesus is led by the Spirit into the ___.

cards.text: Out there, for forty days, the devil tempts Him, and Jesus eats nothing the whole time. FORTY days, friend, and I can't make it forty minutes past the timer without sneaking a cookie off the rack.

cards.question: When the forty days of eating nothing in the wilderness are over, Jesus is hungry.

cards.text: So the devil, who's been tempting Him this whole time, steps up to a hungry Jesus with a dare. Waits till you're at your lowest, then strikes, like the boss who walks over at 4:59 on a Friday and says, "Hey, quick thing."

cards.question: The devil tells Jesus that if He is the Son of God, He should tell this stone to become ___.
Hungry Jesus is staring at a stone the devil wants turned into bread. How does He answer?

answers.text: He answers with what is written
He turns the stone into bread

cards.text: Jesus answers, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’” Forty days without eating, and His comeback is one line. ONE LINE. I need three tries just to say no to the snooze button.
Round two. The devil leads Jesus up to a high place and shows Him all the kingdoms of the world in an instant. In an INSTANT, friend, and it takes me longer than that to find my oven mitt.

cards.question: Up on that high place, the devil offers Jesus authority over all the kingdoms of the world and all their glory.
The devil offers Jesus authority over all the kingdoms and their glory, and says it has been relinquished to him. What does he want from Jesus in return?
Jesus answers the devil's offer with Scripture again. Who does it say to worship and serve?

cards.text: Round three: the devil takes Jesus to Jerusalem, sets Him on the pinnacle of the temple and dares Him, if You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down from here. Friend, I won't even look over the edge of a counter.

cards.question: Up on the pinnacle of the temple, the devil backs up his dare by quoting ___.

cards.text: The devil says it's written that angels will guard Jesus carefully and lift Him up in their hands, so He won't strike His foot against a stone. Wait. WAIT. The devil is quoting Scripture now?

cards.question: Jesus answers the devil's quote with another line of Scripture. What does it say not to do?

answers.text: Put the Lord your God to the test
Stand upon the pinnacle of the temple
Lean on the strength of your own hand

cards.text: Jesus answers, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’” Three temptations, three answers, all from what is written, and back in my blurry days I couldn't go three for three on a straight stamp.

cards.question: When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Jesus for good.

cards.text: When the devil has finished every temptation, he leaves Jesus until an opportune time. That's not goodbye, friend. That's "I'll circle back."

findings.problem: "Waits till you're at your lowest, then strikes" states as fact why the devil chose this moment. Luke 4:2-3 only gives the order of events: Jesus is hungry, then the devil speaks. The text never says the devil waited for Jesus to be at His lowest.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The question asks "How does He answer?" The right answer "He answers with what is written" is the only option that repeats the question's verb and is actually a way of answering. The other two are actions. This makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The core action in the fact is the devil showing Jesus all the kingdoms in an instant. The comparison is about searching for an oven mitt, which is a different action. The joke only shares the idea of speed, so it doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer "Scripture" is a text. The wrong answers "priests" and "elders" are groups of people, so they aren't the same kind of thing. "quoting priests" and "quoting elders" also read awkwardly next to "quoting Scripture."

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Three temptations, three answers" says there were only three temptations. Luke 4:2 says Jesus was tempted by the devil for forty days, and 4:13 says "every temptation." Luke records three exchanges, but the text doesn't limit the temptations to three. Wording like "three answers" or "three times" would stay true to the text.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.
